title: SNPs and genotypes

blocks.what_we_do: Distinguish a DNA site, an allele and a genotype.
blocks.why: A variant is a position where DNA differs between people. An allele is one of its possible sequences. A single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) has single-base alternatives. At an ordinary autosomal site a person carries two copies: an A/G site can have A/A, A/G or G/G genotypes. Missing is not a fourth allele. X, Y and mitochondrial DNA need different copy-number assumptions, discussed at 4.5.
blocks.command:
```{r s1-1}
ann <- guided_table(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "array", "sim2026_array_annotation.tsv"))
head(ann[c("Name", "Chr", "Position_GRCh38", "Ref_Plus", "Alt_Plus")])
```

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
A table of site identifiers, chromosome, GRCh38 coordinate and plus-strand alleles. The annotation contains 299,523 rows. Array site names are not guaranteed to be rs identifiers.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows with the supplied simulated dataset.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
At a C/T autosomal site, does C/T represent two variants or one genotype?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

One genotype at one variant: one C allele and one T allele.

</details>
